C-BROWSER-PROVIDER-ROUTING-BUDGET-REMEDI.Summary:
Remediate two audit findings at the M1.2 browser provider boundary without reopening unrelated browser architecture: restore finite-budget guarantees already claimed by the applied M1.2 GRACE contract, and preserve explicit browser capability identity across the native provider IPC path so routing never infers a contract from payload shape.
The change also closes the verification gap that allowed configured but unenforced limits to appear covered by a broadly named acceptance test. Historical applied bundles remain unchanged; this remediation produces fresh evidence instead of rewriting prior claims.
C-BROWSER-PROVIDER-ROUTING-BUDGET-REMEDI.Problem:
The applied M1.2 specification requires exact production budgets to be finite, startup-validated and testable through injected small limits, with explicit bounded failure on exhaustion. BrowserProviderCore currently exposes ProviderBudgetLimits.max_contexts and ProviderBudgetLimits.max_pages_per_context, but does not enforce either limit. The existing provider_budget_limits_enforcement test injects small values for those fields but exercises only max_action_text_len. A green test can therefore coexist with decorative resource-policy fields.
Separately, the native browser provider serializes capability requests as operation plus opaque payload and drops browser contract identity before BrowserProviderCore routing. Multiple contracts intentionally reuse operation names such as create, close and list. BrowserProviderCore resolves those bare operations by inspecting payload fields even though the architecture already defines explicit contract boundaries and dispatch_contract accepts contract and operation separately.
These findings do not establish a demonstrated authorization bypass. They do establish a contract/evidence mismatch and an avoidable protocol ambiguity at a security-sensitive native boundary.

Goals.Goal: Enforce max_contexts and max_pages_per_context with deterministic explicit limit failures before creating excess engine resources.
Audit every finite-budget claim named by the applied M1.2 browser-provider contract and record its authoritative owner, enforcement point and executable evidence.
Carry explicit browser contract identity together with operation and payload across the native browser-provider capability request path.
Make dispatch_contract or an equivalent explicit contract-plus-operation router the single authoritative browser-provider routing truth.
Remove payload-shape inference for ambiguous bare operations such as create, close and list.
Retain only bounded, explicit and test-covered compatibility aliases; compatibility routing must not create a second semantic dispatch implementation.
Add acceptance tests whose assertions independently prove each repaired budget and ambiguous routing case rather than relying on test names or configuration presence.
Preserve the real CEF provider, reference fixture, browser service plugins, stable Browser Contract v1.0 semantics and existing experimental 0.1/0.2 surfaces.
Preserve historical applied M1.2/M1.3 bundles as historical evidence and close this audit through a new GRACE change.

Constraints.Constraint: SPEC APPROVAL AND EXACT PLAN APPROVAL REMAIN SEPARATE; THIS DRAFT DOES NOT AUTHORIZE IMPLEMENTATION.
DO NOT EDIT ARCHIVED M1.2 OR M1.3 BUNDLES TO PRETEND THE MISSING BUDGET ASSERTIONS OR ROUTING IDENTITY WERE PREVIOUSLY PROVEN.
THE ACTIVE REQUEST-POLICY/INTERCEPTION CHANGE IS OUT OF SCOPE EXCEPT THAT ITS FUTURE CALLERS MUST INHERIT THE REPAIRED GENERIC BROWSER-PROVIDER ROUTING BOUNDARY.
STABLE Browser Contract v1.0 REQUEST/RESPONSE WIRE FORMS MUST NOT BE INCOMPATIBLY REDEFINED.
EXISTING EXPERIMENTAL browser.capture, browser.engine.cookies AND browser.engine.storage CONTRACTS MUST NOT BE REINTERPRETED IN PLACE.
CAPABILITY CONTRACT IDENTITY MUST BE EXPLICIT AT THE PROVIDER ROUTING BOUNDARY; PAYLOAD KEYS, VALUES OR SHAPE MUST NOT SELECT THE CONTRACT.
AMBIGUOUS OPERATION-ONLY REQUESTS MUST FAIL CLOSED OR PASS THROUGH A SEPARATELY NAMED LEGACY ADAPTER THAT DOES NOT INSPECT PAYLOAD SHAPE.
ONE CANONICAL ROUTING TABLE OWNS CONTRACT-PLUS-OPERATION SEMANTICS. COMPATIBILITY ALIASES MAY NORMALIZE INTO THAT TABLE BUT MUST NOT DUPLICATE BACKEND DISPATCH LOGIC.
ANY TEMPORARY LEGACY ALIAS MUST HAVE A KNOWN CALLER, AN ACCEPTANCE TEST AND AN EXPLICIT REMOVAL CONDITION.
RESOURCE LIMITS MUST BE ENFORCED BEFORE THE CORRESPONDING RESOURCE-CREATING SIDE EFFECT WHEN PRACTICABLE; LIMIT FAILURE MUST NOT LEAK A PARTIALLY CREATED CONTEXT OR PAGE.
INJECTED SMALL LIMITS MUST EXERCISE THE SAME ENFORCEMENT PATH USED BY DEFAULT PRODUCTION LIMITS.
REFERENCE AND CEF BACKENDS MUST OBSERVE THE SAME PROVIDER-LEVEL CONTEXT/PAGE LIMIT SEMANTICS; A BACKEND MAY ENFORCE TIGHTER INTERNAL LIMITS BUT MAY NOT BYPASS PROVIDER POLICY.
BUDGET AUDIT EVIDENCE MUST DISTINGUISH PROVIDER-CORE LIMITS, NATIVE-HOST/IPC LIMITS, QUERY/CAPTURE BOUNDS AND ENGINE-INTERNAL BOUNDS RATHER THAN COLLAPSING THEM INTO ONE GREEN TEST.
NO BROWSER-SPECIFIC KERNEL PRIVILEGE OR IPC BYPASS MAY BE INTRODUCED.
NO BROAD HELPER-CLEANUP, STYLE REWRITE OR UNRELATED CRATE REORGANIZATION IS AUTHORIZED BY THIS CHANGE.
EXISTING REAL CEF, S2, S3B, ARCHITECTURE-SECURITY AND COMPATIBILITY GATES MUST NOT BE WEAKENED OR SKIPPED TO MAKE THE REMEDIATION GREEN.
GRACE STATUS MAY NOT ADVANCE TO applied UNTIL FRESH REQUIRED LOCAL/HOSTED EVIDENCE IS GREEN AND THE OWNER EXPLICITLY CONFIRMS APPLY.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Changing the selected browser engine or CEF packaging strategy.
Redesigning tabs, history, downloads, cookies, site-data or Shell UI.
Promoting experimental browser contracts to stable v1.
Removing every short helper or adapter in the browser workspace.
Changing generic native IPC envelope framing or PROTOCOL_VERSION unless the approved plan proves an additive browser-provider payload change cannot be expressed inside the existing opaque payload.
Claiming that the current routing ambiguity is an exploited authorization vulnerability without separate evidence.
Re-auditing every historical GRACE change in this bundle.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: ProviderBudgetLimits.max_contexts is enforced on context creation; with an injected limit of 2, the first two contexts succeed, the third fails with an explicit bounded/limit error, and list_contexts reports exactly two created contexts.

ProviderBudgetLimits.max_pages_per_context is enforced per BrowserContextId; with an injected limit of 2, the first two pages in one context succeed, the third fails explicitly, and another context retains its own independent page budget.

Closing a context or page releases the corresponding provider-level budget occupancy according to documented lifecycle semantics, and tests prove a replacement resource can be created afterward when capacity is available.
A failed context/page limit check occurs before the backend resource-creating operation or otherwise proves rollback/no-leak semantics through backend-observable acceptance evidence.
ProviderBudgetLimits zero-value semantics are explicit and tested: either startup rejects nonsensical limits or zero is intentionally defined as deny-all.
The existing max_action_text_len behavior remains enforced and receives an assertion independent from the new context/page budget assertions.

A repository-owned browser-provider budget evidence matrix maps every finite-budget claim from the applied M1.2 specification to an owner, implementation location, configured/default limit and concrete acceptance test or explicitly identifies a separately owned bound.

The budget matrix specifically accounts for contexts, pages, pending native RPC/in-flight calls, native frame size, query bounds, capture bounds, event/download buffering or mailboxes, startup/shutdown deadlines and any provider dispatch queue claimed by M1.2.
No budget is reported as enforced solely because a configuration field, constant, constructor argument or test fixture value exists.
The native browser-provider CapabilityPayload or its approved replacement carries explicit browser contract identity in addition to operation and payload.
The normal native provider path routes explicit contract plus operation to dispatch_contract or an equivalent single canonical router without inferring contract identity from payload contents.
Requests for browser.context/create and browser.page/create remain distinguishable even when supplied payloads share, omit or maliciously add fields that previously influenced heuristic routing.

Bare ambiguous operation-only create, close and list requests no longer inspect payload shape. They either fail explicitly as ambiguous or are accepted only through a separately named legacy form whose contract identity is unambiguous.
Unknown contract names, unknown operations and invalid contract-operation pairs fail closed and never fall through to a different browser contract because the payload happens to deserialize there.
Authorization/resource-scope checks remain outside payload-controlled routing and existing authority-separation acceptance tests stay green.
Compatibility aliases, if retained, normalize at one boundary into canonical contract-plus-operation values; backend dispatch semantics are not duplicated across alias tables.

The out-of-process provider acceptance suite sends explicit contract identity and proves context create, page create, navigation, observe, query, action, capture and engine primitive calls through the repaired native path.
The real Windows S2/S3B proving paths use the repaired explicit contract identity and do not rely on payload-shape inference.
Reference fixtures may retain convenience helpers, but production evidence does not use an operation-only ambiguous route.
Stable Browser Contract v1.0 JSON compatibility fixtures and experimental 0.1/0.2 compatibility tests remain green without reinterpreting existing public DTO semantics.
scripts/ci/Test-WorldlineArchitecture.ps1 or an equivalent repository-owned static check rejects reintroduction of payload-shape contract inference in the browser-provider routing path.
Provider budget tests are structured so removal of max_contexts or max_pages_per_context enforcement makes a named test fail, independent of max_action_text_len.
GRACE verification projection for the remediated browser-provider boundary references the new evidence instead of treating historical M1.2 green status as proof of the repaired assertions.

Fresh local Source, Correctness, ArchitectureSecurity, BrowserProvider, ProvingSlice and All suites are green; required Windows real-provider gates are green where the changed native routing path participates.
This change remains draft/approved/executing according to the normal GRACE lifecycle and is not applied or archived as successful until required evidence and explicit owner apply confirmation exist.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh evidence names exact injected context/page saturation tests, lifecycle capacity-release tests, explicit contract-plus-operation native IPC tests, ambiguous-operation negative tests, an architecture check preventing payload-shape routing, the budget ownership/evidence matrix, and the hosted Windows real-provider run required by the final approved plan.

Assumptions.Assumption: The current master implementation remains materially as audited: BrowserProviderCore exposes max_contexts and max_pages_per_context without enforcing them, while max_action_text_len is enforced.

The current native browser provider capability payload carries operation and payload but not explicit browser contract identity, and the provider process dispatches through BrowserProviderCore::dispatch.

BrowserProviderCore::dispatch_contract is the existing explicit contract-plus-operation seam and can be retained or replaced by an equivalent single canonical router without changing stable browser contract semantics.
The worldline-plugin-protocol Envelope payload remains protocol-opaque, so an additive browser-provider payload shape can normally be introduced without changing generic envelope framing.
Native host max_in_flight and frame-size controls are separately implemented generic bounds; the plan must verify rather than duplicate them in BrowserProviderCore.
The active request-policy/interception bundle remains independently governed and may be rebased on the repaired provider boundary after this remediation if sequencing requires it.
The implementation plan may split budget remediation, routing migration, compatibility cleanup and verification hardening into dependency-ordered tasks under this one change.
